text: {"score":3,"justification":"Most numbers match the card (11.9%, 4.3%, 6.45, 1.37, 19%, 45 records, 18 99215 docs, 1 below, 40/3). But the summary's conclusion is weakly supported and internally tense. It leans 'high-acuity panel' and 'do not pursue' while its own figures show the 99215 share is 2.75x expected and about 148 excess claims. A 45-claim sample (2.3% of claims) is thin for dismissing the case. The summary also misses the card's by-complexity data, which cuts both ways. Cited claims fit their sentences, but C0297152 is a low-complexity patient with high-MDM documentation, which is used appropriately. The unmatched '24%' is the 'problems' share from note checks that is not on the card; it is not explained, and the summary does not say what 'problems' means.","problems":["Conclusion 'do not pursue recovery' and 'sampled documentation supports billed level' overreaches from 18 documented 99215 claims (about 8% of 232) and a 2.3% documentation sample.","Headline says 'mostly support' and the leaning calls it a high-acuity panel, yet the 2.75x ratio to expected and about 148 excess 99215 claims are not addressed; z of 1.37 is modest, but the risk-adjusted excess remains.","The 24% 'problems' figure is not on the card and is not explained; the note-check figures are provided without interpretation.","High-acuity panel framing is not backed by numbers: the by-complexity table shows 99215 shares above all-provider rates in every complexity band, which suggests a higher level at the same complexity. The summary does not mention this.","Comparison rate of 9% below billed is quoted without noting that the provider's 6% is based on a single claim.","Next steps are generic and offer no targeted request, for example expanding the sample toward low-complexity 99215 claims. Few of the 25 low-complexity claims were documented.","The sample's selection method is not discussed, so it may be unrepresentative of the low-complexity 99215 claims."]}
